note: To measure ONE census metric cost without per-metric instrumentation, difference two lab studies over the same seed panel: a hot study selecting only that metric, and a control study selecting one cheap ledger-scan metric (first-day-is-settlement). Both build identical worlds, so build cost cancels and the difference IS the metric. Run them interleaved, several reps, and report CPU-seconds not wall - the Mac was at load 6.5/10 throughout and CPU-s still gave 0.9-1.8 percent spread. Measured for history-myth-hop-median: control 91.66 then 91.65 CPU-s across the change (unmoved, which is what makes the delta attributable), hot 159.98 then 91.56. Metric went 1.708 CPU-s/world to below the noise floor. Studies under 200 projected world builds skip the heavy-writer claim, so a 40-seed panel runs free; a 1000-seed panel takes the claim and cost 305 s wall / 2269 CPU-s. Same rows.csv render path as the census, so the probe output diffs directly against the committed census column.
